summary: Semaglutide is a peptide in the incretin & amylin analogs class (GLP-1 receptor agonist). Europe PMC indexes 6,039 publications naming it or a listed alias in a title or abstract, including 305 randomized controlled trials and 198 clinical trials of any design, as of 2026-09-09. The strongest evidence tier in that literature is an approved medicine with a regulator-reviewed label. This page reports what those studies state, sentence by sentence, with each statement tied to its source and labeled by the kind of evidence it is. It does not recommend use, and it does not translate study doses into anything personal.

faq.question: Has Semaglutide been tested in humans?
faq.answer: Yes. Europe PMC indexes 198 clinical trials and 305 randomized controlled trials naming Semaglutide or a listed alias in the title or abstract. The evidence table above lists the ones in this record's ledger with their design and sample size; check the study name, since an alias can refer to a different formulation of the same molecule.

faq.question: What kind of evidence exists for Semaglutide?
faq.answer: The strongest tier is approved label: an approved medicine with a regulator-reviewed label. Every claim on this page carries its own tier, because a compound with one human trial and forty animal studies is described by both facts, not the better one.

faq.question: Is Semaglutide an approved medicine?
faq.answer: ChEMBL records CHEMBL2108724 at maximum clinical phase 4, first approved 2017. Approval status differs by jurisdiction and is pending human review on this record.

faq.question: Which species has Semaglutide been studied in?
faq.answer: Studies in this record's ledger report work in: Humans. Findings in one species do not transfer to another, and weight-normalized doses in particular do not scale linearly between them.
